basic_details.job_title: MHA Police Reform Coordinator Recruitment 2027 – Apply Online
basic_details.short_information: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Government of India, has invited nominations of serving police officers in the rank of DIG/IG or equivalent for secondment to the United Nations post of Police Reform Coordinator, P-5 in the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA), Bangui. The nominations go through proper channel and must be sent by email to [email protected] and [email protected]. Applications received after 15 January 2027 will not be considered.

qualification.details: The UN Job Opening 2026-MINUSCA-89650-DPO dated 27 October 2026 sets these requirements for the Police Reform Coordinator, P-5: | Education: Advanced university degree (Masters or equivalent) in law, police management, law enforcement, security studies, criminal justice, business or public administration, program management, change management, or related area. A first level university degree with a combination of relevant academic qualifications and extensive experience in law enforcement, in the areas of management, planning and administration may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Graduation from a certified Police Academy or other national or international Law Enforcement Training Institution is required. Experience: Candidate must be in active police service with a minimum of 10 years (12 years in absence of advanced degree) of progressive relevant and active policing experience in a national or international law enforcement agency, at the field and/or national police headquarters level. Seven (7) years of active police experience at senior policy making level, including strategic planning and management experience in one or few of: police operations, crime management, police administration, police training and development, change management (particularly in law enforcement) – required. Rank: MHA asks for officers in the rank of DIG/IG or equivalent; the UN Job Opening lists Chief Superintendent of Police, Colonel, other equivalent or higher rank. Language: Fluency in oral and written French is required. Knowledge of English is highly desirable. | Specialized training in the area of the incumbent's responsibility (reform, strategic planning, administration, training) is highly desirable. Practical direct experience in commanding a regional or a state level police unit, or heading a unit at national police HQ level – desired. Practical experience in institutional building, reforming and restructuring in law enforcement or a related field is highly desirable. Previous UN or international experience is an advantage. | Candidates must meet all the requirements of the Job Opening at the time of nomination. Nomination of eligible women officers is strongly encouraged. The post carries the UN level P-5; the notice does not mention the pay amount. Candidates should check the full UN Job Opening enclosed with the official notification for the complete eligibility text.

selection_process: The selection decision is taken by the United Nations. The final decision on selecting an individual is also subject to human rights screening. Candidates approved for the roster may be selected for positions with similar functions (same functional title and level) without a new Job Opening
and remain on the roster for two years after the first day of the month following the selection decision.
important_instructions: Nominations without Vigilance clearance and Cadre clearance (for all officers) will be summarily rejected. No format other than the enclosed specimen (duly typed) will be accepted; hand-written PHP will not be accepted. Secondment is for an initial one year, with possible extension for a second and third year; in exceptional circumstances a fourth year, but not longer. During secondment, police personnel are not eligible for reassignment or transfer to any other seconded position. Currently serving active-duty seconded police personnel on a UN staff contract will not be considered; earlier seconded officers may reapply after a break of at least one year. Officers should not make direct queries with MHA or UNHQ regarding selection; MHA will not entertain personal queries from individual applicants. For enquiries the notice prints the telephone 011-24010236 (Deepak Sharma, Under Secretary).

content_sections.heading: About the Notice
content_sections.text: The circular is issued by the Pers. Policy Section of the Police-II Division, Ministry of Home Affairs, Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. It forwards a vacancy announcement received from the Ministry of External Affairs through the Permanent Mission of India to the United Nations (PMI to UN). The post is advertised by the UN Department of Peace Operations (DPO) for MINUSCA, a peacekeeping mission whose posts are financed by the support account of peacekeeping operations.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Individual officers do not apply directly. Nominations of eligible and willing officers are forwarded through proper channel to MHA: State officers: through the Home Department of the State concerned. Officers of organisations: with the approval of the Head of Organisation. AGMUT cadre officers: through the UT Division, MHA. The Chief Secretaries of UTs and the Commissioner of Police, Delhi have been told that nominations are to be submitted through the UT Division, MHA only. All documents of each nominated candidate must be compiled in a separate single file (PDF format only) and emailed to [email protected] and [email protected] before 15 January 2027. Under the Digital India initiative, documents are sent in digital mode only and no hard or physical copies are required. The notice does not prescribe an email subject line.

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: The UN Job Opening 2026-MINUSCA-89650-DPO dated 27 October 2026 sets these requirements for the Police Reform Coordinator, P-5: Education: Advanced university degree (Masters or equivalent) in law, police management, law enforcement, security studies, criminal justice, business or public administration, program management, change management, or related area. A first level university degree with a combination of relevant academic qualifications and extensive experience in law enforcement, in the areas of management, planning and administration may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Graduation from a certified Police Academy or other national or international Law Enforcement Training Institution is required. Experience: Candidate must be in active police service with a minimum of 10 years (12 years in absence of advanced degree) of progressive relevant and active policing experience in a national or international law enforcement agency, at the field and/or national police headquarters level. Seven (7) years of active police experience at senior policy making level, including strategic planning and management experience in one or few of: police operations, crime management, police administration, police training and development, change management (particularly in law enforcement) – required. Rank: MHA asks for officers in the rank of DIG/IG or equivalent; the UN Job Opening lists Chief Superintendent of Police, Colonel, other equivalent or higher rank. Language: Fluency in oral and written French is required. Knowledge of English is highly desirable. Specialized training in the area of the incumbent's responsibility (reform, strategic planning, administration, training) is highly desirable. Practical direct experience in commanding a regional or a state level police unit, or heading a unit at national police HQ level – desired. Practical experience in institutional building, reforming and restructuring in law enforcement or a related field is highly desirable. Previous UN or international experience is an advantage. Candidates must meet all the requirements of the Job Opening at the time of nomination. Nomination of eligible women officers is strongly encouraged. The post carries the UN level P-5; the notice does not mention the pay amount. Candidates should check the full UN Job Opening enclosed with the official notification for the complete eligibility text.

content_sections.heading: MHA Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: Under the guidance and supervision of the Police Commissioner, the Reform Coordinator is responsible for the development of the Police and Gendarmerie in the Central African Republic. Duties as printed include: Review the existing local Police and Gendarmerie structure and systems, including personnel and skills requirements and the criminal justice system, as the basis for reform recommendations. Develop plans, programs and project proposals for the reform, restructuring and institutional development of the National Police and Gendarmerie; propose fund-raising initiatives on international funding. Advise and assist local counterparts on reform initiatives and on recruitment, vetting and selection policies and procedures. Conduct periodic evaluation of all reform activities and coordinate bilateral and multilateral support for security sector reform. Liaise with senior National Police and Gendarmerie officials and other government officials on restructuring or setting up infrastructures. Lead the formation, supervision and coordination of UNPOL training; develop a training database; produce and submit reports on reform and training. Make periodic assessments of MINUSCA Police and Gendarmerie officers' performance and chair periodic meetings with UNPOL Chiefs. Supervise assigned administrative staff and UNPOL personnel, ensure efficient use of mission police assets, and perform other duties assigned by the Police Commissioner or Deputy. The officer reports to the Police Commissioner. The competencies listed are Professionalism, Planning and organizing, Client Orientation and Leadership.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: United Nations Personal History Profile (PHP) form (P.11), duly completed, typed (not hand-written) and signed, with the photograph on the front side and signature on the last page. United Nations Employment and Academic Certification (EAC), signed by the candidate and the Designated Authority of the concerned Force; an EAC without that signature results in rejection. Personal details as per Annexure-II (Bio-Data Proforma with recent passport size photograph). APAR/ACR gradings of the last five years (mandatory) in the forwarding letter – only gradings, no copies of APAR/ACR. Human Rights Certificate in the prescribed wording, signed by an officer not below the rank of DIG/Director. Signed self-attestation in the prescribed format.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The selection decision is taken by the United Nations. The final decision on selecting an individual is also subject to human rights screening. Candidates approved for the roster may be selected for positions with similar functions (same functional title and level) without a new Job Opening, and remain on the roster for two years after the first day of the month following the selection decision.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date for MHA Police Reform Coordinator nominations?
faq.answer: Nominations must reach MHA by 15 January 2027; applications received after this date will not be considered.

faq.question: Q2. Who can be nominated for the Police Reform Coordinator, P-5 post?
faq.answer: Officers in active police service in the rank of DIG/IG or equivalent who meet the UN Job Opening criteria can be nominated through proper channel.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required?
faq.answer: An advanced university degree (Masters or equivalent) in a related area, or a first level degree with relevant qualifications and extensive law enforcement experience, plus graduation from a certified Police Academy or Law Enforcement Training Institution.

faq.question: Q4. How much experience is needed?
faq.answer: A minimum of 10 years (12 years in absence of advanced degree) of active policing experience, including seven years at senior policy making level.

faq.question: Q5. Is French mandatory for this UN post?
faq.answer: Yes, fluency in oral and written French is required, and knowledge of English is highly desirable.

faq.question: Q6. How are the nominations sent?
faq.answer: All documents are compiled in a single PDF and emailed through proper channel to [email protected] and [email protected]; no hard copies are required.

faq.question: Q7. What documents are needed?
faq.answer: The P-11 form, EAC, Annexure-II bio-data, APAR/ACR gradings of the last five years, the Human Rights Certificate and a signed self-attestation.

faq.question: Q8. How long is the secondment?
faq.answer: The initial period is 12 months (extendible), with possible extension for a second and third year and, in exceptional circumstances, a fourth year but not longer.

faq.question: Q9. Will a nomination without vigilance clearance be accepted?
faq.answer: No, nominations without Vigilance clearance and Cadre clearance will be summarily rejected.
